Jezreel (Place)
JEZ-ree-ul
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Yizre'el (H3157), "God sows" or "God scatters/plants," from zara ("to sow") + El ("God"). A city and fertile valley in northern Israel; the site of Ahab's palace and Naboth's vineyard.

📖 Biblical Definition

Jezreel ("God sows") was a city and the broad, fertile valley in northern Israel that served as a second royal residence for King Ahab, and which became the scene of some of the most infamous bloodshed of the divided kingdom. It was at Jezreel that Naboth had his vineyard, which Ahab coveted; when Naboth refused to sell his ancestral inheritance, Queen Jezebel arranged his judicial murder by false witnesses, and Ahab took possession — whereupon Elijah met him in the vineyard with the LORD's terrible word of judgment: "In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine" (1 Kings 21:19), and concerning Jezebel, "The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel" (1 Kings 21:23). These prophecies were fulfilled at Jezreel years later when Jehu, anointed to destroy the house of Ahab, came to the city: he shot Ahab's son Joram and cast his body into the portion of Naboth's field (2 Kings 9:24-26), and he had Jezebel thrown down from her window, where the dogs ate her flesh as Elijah had foretold (2 Kings 9:30-37). At Jezreel also the seventy sons of Ahab were slain and their heads piled at the gate (2 Kings 10). Jezreel thus became a byword for the blood of the house of Ahab and the judgment of God upon dynastic wickedness. The prophet Hosea was commanded to name his first son Jezreel, "for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu" (Hos 1:4) — for Jehu, though he executed God's judgment, had himself shed blood with wrong motives and continued in the sins of Jeroboam. Yet the same name, "God sows," carries a note of hope: Hosea also foretells a day of restoration when "great shall be the day of Jezreel" and God will sow His people in the land in mercy (Hos 1:11; 2:22-23). Jezreel is thus a place of both judgment and the promise of restoration — God sowing in wrath, and God sowing in mercy.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A city and fertile valley in northern Israel, Ahab's second royal seat; scene of Naboth's vineyard and judicial murder, Elijah's judgment, and Jehu's slaughter of the house of Ahab and Jezebel (1 Kings 21; 2 Kings 9-10); a byword for bloodshed, yet its name ("God sows") carries the promise of restoration (Hosea).

JEZREEL (PLACE), proper noun. Hebrew Yizre'el (H3157), "God sows"; a city and fertile valley in northern Israel.

Ahab's second royal residence; site of Naboth's vineyard, which Ahab coveted and Jezebel seized by judicial murder (1 Kings 21).

Elijah pronounced judgment there: dogs would lick Ahab's blood and eat Jezebel (1 Kings 21:19, 23).

Jehu fulfilled it: Joram slain and cast into Naboth's field, Jezebel thrown down and eaten by dogs, Ahab's seventy sons slain (2 Kings 9-10).

Hosea named a son Jezreel for the blood-guilt (Hos 1:4), yet foretold restoration: "great shall be the day of Jezreel" (Hos 1:11).

📖 Key Scripture

1 Kings 21:19 — "And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession?... In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine."

1 Kings 21:23 — "And of Jezebel also spake the LORD, saying, The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel."

2 Kings 9:36-37 — "This is the word of the LORD, which he spake by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel shall dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel."

Hosea 1:4-5 — "Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Jezreel is corrupted when its bloodshed is read as mere ancient dynastic violence, when the certainty of God's judgment on wickedness is softened, or when the double meaning of the name (judgment and restoration) is missed.

expand to see more

Judgment-certainty softened. The story of Jezreel is, above all, a demonstration that God's pronounced judgment certainly comes to pass, however long delayed. Elijah spoke the word against Ahab and Jezebel in the vineyard; years passed; Ahab even humbled himself for a time, delaying the judgment to his son's days (1 Kings 21:29); but in the end every word was fulfilled to the letter at Jezreel — the dogs licked the blood, the dogs ate Jezebel, the house of Ahab was cut off. The lesson is sobering: God's patience is not God's forgetfulness, and His delayed judgment is not His abandoned judgment. What He has spoken against wickedness He will perform, in His time, exactly as He said.

Jezreel has no significant postmodern redefinition. The principal point worth recovering is the double meaning carried in its name, "God sows." Jezreel was the place where God sowed judgment — the blood of Ahab's house, repaid for the blood of Naboth and the prophets. Yet through Hosea the same name becomes a word of hope: a day is coming when God will sow His scattered people back into the land in mercy, when "great shall be the day of Jezreel" (Hos 1:11) and He will say to Lo-ammi, "Thou art my people" (Hos 2:23). The God who sows in wrath also sows in mercy; the place of judgment becomes, in the promise, the place of restoration. So the gospel turns even Jezreel from a byword of blood into a token of the mercy by which God gathers a people to Himself.
